pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/app/report/[owner]/[repo]/opengraph-image.doors.test.ts:11 The permalink's social card is JSX for an outside renderer (next/og / satori) that has its own rules, and the only tests of this route swap that renderer for a recorder (the share-card failure test makes it throw), so no lane checks that the renderer accepts the real card. That leaves the route's 'an unfurl can NEVER fail' claim (opengraph-image.tsx:12) asserted only on the near side.

techniques.evidence: src/app/report/[owner]/[repo]/opengraph-image.doors.test.ts:11 The test reads which card element was built 'without rasterising anything'. The renderer is available in the lane and is never run on the real ReportShareCard.

src/app/report/[owner]/[repo]/page.unreachable.test.tsx:9 The file names the producer the earlier tests asserted against and now runs the real readers and dbReadSafe, so the null-on-outage decision is actually reached.
src/app/report/[owner]/[repo]/page.unreachable.test.tsx:30 The only fake is the Prisma client. The shipped reader and wrapper chain is used instead of a convenience stub that forks it.

pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/components/landing/prism/PrismHero.tsx:48 The Prism redesign changed the hero h1 and turned 'Scan a repository' into a link (PrismScanLink), but the live-app smoke that CI and the post-deploy job run still finds the hero by old copy and an old role. The harness was not moved with the product, and the landing's only live-lane check cannot pass against the shipped page.

techniques.evidence: e2e/scan.spec.ts:11 The test finds the hero by display copy, not a stable identifier. That copy no longer exists anywhere in src, and the visible CTA is now a link, not a button (scan.spec.ts:13). The product changed without its harness.
src/components/landing/prism/PrismLadder.dom.test.tsx:12 The swap beat is flushed by advancing fake timers, not by waiting on real time.
src/components/landing/prism/PrismLanding.smoke.test.tsx:14 The stub says what it leaves out and limits its claim to mounting.
